title: First Sealand Dynasty
capsule: The First Sealand Dynasty (also called the Second Dynasty of Babylon) was an independent polity that ruled southern Mesopotamia's marshy lowlands near the mouths of the Tigris and Euphrates from roughly the 18th to 15th centuries BCE, contemporary with and opposed to Amorite Babylon. Its founder Ilum-ma-ilī defeated the Babylonian king Samsu-iluna's army, and the dynasty maintained independence through eleven successive rulers across roughly two and a half centuries. The last king Ea-gâmil fled to Elam when the Kassite chief Ulam-Buriaš conquered the Sealand around 1475 BCE and incorporated it into the growing Kassite dominion over Babylonia.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The dynasty is attested through king lists and a single administrative tablet archive (the Sealand Archive purchased by the British Museum); territorial extent in the southern marshes is inferred from these sources and is not archaeologically mapped with precision.
